To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we present a novel framework for image semantic segmentation that exploits local patch aspect coherence and weak neighbours; 2) we propose a novel strategy for efficient inference in CRFs; and 3) we show that our framework outperforms the state of the art in the field of image semantic segmentation.
we propose a new framework that jointly learns image category appearance and pixel dependencies at multiple scales.

(i) the joint learning of category appearances and pixel relationships at different scales improves the performance of semantic image labelling; (ii) the introduction of a novel strategy to impose aspect coherence in the CRF graph leads to exact inference; and (iii) the introduction of ‘weak neighbours’ allows to exploit patch neighbourhood information without introducing loops in CRF graphs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of new methods for the semantic segmentation of images.
developing new methods for the analysis of visual data.
the development of a new framework for semantic image labelling based on a graph representation of image patches.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper presents a new approach to the semantic image labelling problem, which is able to exploit different scales of pixel dependency and to achieve good results.
a novel method for semantic segmentation of images is presented, that exploits local patch aspect coherence in a conditional random field.
the proposed method is a good example of how the use of graph structures and the use of a CRF framework can lead to good results.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a novel framework for semantic image labelling that is able to jointly account for different types of image dependencies at different scales, while maintaining an efficient inference.
we propose a method to exploit local patch appearance and aspect coherence to improve the performance of a CRF-based approach to semantic image labelling.
we have proposed a new method for image labelling that jointly learns the visual appearance of categories and the spatial relationships between them.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of local and contextual information can lead to improved semantic labelling results.

the combination of image oversegmentation, aspect coherence and weak neighbours is an effective strategy to learn pixel dependencies at different scale levels and to exploit the resulting information for image segmentation.
a CRF model can be used as a powerful tool to model dependencies at different scales and to exploit aspect coherence to improve inference.
